solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Son on edge could be a biblical one

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
a hem is the finished edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A nervous son, perhaps one straight out of the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the S first, above the edge. 'One' in the definition refers back to 'Son', so the answer is a biblical son.
explanation.definitionFit: Shem was the eldest son of Noah in Genesis, so he is a son found in the Bible.

clue.text: Doctor restricting exercise forgiven

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so the doctor's letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: ScD is a Doctor of Science
to exercise a right or power is to use it

explanation.surface: A doctor limits a patient's workouts and is then pardoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' here is not the usual DR or MO but the degree ScD.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Scused is an archaic clipped form of excused, as in Shakespeare, meaning pardoned or let off.

clue.text: More than one Cobra improved heady Madras

indicators.note: something improved has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Cobra beer seems to make a fiery Madras curry better.
explanation.walkthrough: Cobra is a beer served in Indian restaurants, which suits the curry, but here it is the snake. The capital C hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamadryad is the king cobra, and hamadryades is one of its plural forms.

clue.text: Traditional courtyard meeting about breaking horse

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece goes in the middle of the other

blocks.note: a mare is a female horse
Chambers gives a as an abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: An old courtyard gathering is held to discuss breaking in a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meeting' reads as part of the definition but simply joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A marae is the enclosed open space in front of a Maori meeting house, used for traditional ceremonies.

clue.text: Works unattributed as notepad somehow lacking name

indicators.note: lacking something means it is missing, so a letter is dropped
somehow suggests things happen in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to work with
N is the abbreviation for name, the letter to remove

explanation.surface: Writings jotted in a notepad without any author's name attached.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N out of AS NOTEPAD and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Adespota are literary works of unknown authorship, from Greek for 'without a master'.

clue.text: See me alas on the outside getting loss of honour

indicators.note: being on the outside means wrapping around something, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: ay is an old exclamation of sorrow, like alas
the setter is Tim Moorey, so 'me' is his name

explanation.surface: Someone sadly summons a person over a public disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter refers to himself: 'me' is Tim, and AY wraps round him.
explanation.definitionFit: Atimy, from Greek atimia, was public disgrace in ancient Athens, the formal loss of a citizen's rights and honour.

clue.text: European music reviewer of rock

blocks.note: EU is the European Union
a reviewer of music is a critic

explanation.surface: A Continental journalist reviews rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like the music the critic reviews, but it is geology.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucritic describes eucrite, a type of igneous rock, so it means relating to that stone.

clue.text: Endless pasta almost entirely fresher

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: penne is tube-shaped pasta
entirely means all

explanation.surface: A first-year student, nearly all of whose meals are endless pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennal was a first-year student at a German university, so it is an old term for a fresher, or freshman.

clue.text: Utter a couple of instructions to leave

definitions.text: a couple of instructions to leave

blocks.note: first meaning: complete, thoroughgoing

blocks.clueFragment: a couple of instructions to leave
blocks.note: second meaning: two orders to get out, joined by 'and'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like a verb meaning say, but it is the adjective. The second meaning is a playful reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-and-out is an adjective for complete or absolute, as in an out-and-out lie.

clue.text: High places in Scottish resort that's special

blocks.note: Ayr is a seaside town on the west coast of Scotland
i.e. stands for id est, that is
S is an abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A Scottish holiday town that has something special in its hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayries is a variant spelling of eyries, the nests of birds of prey built on high crags.

clue.text: Fruit basket needing thin strip of wood in cases taken by American

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
taken by puts the second piece after, as if received in turn

blocks.note: Chambers gives ca. as an abbreviation for cases
a lath is a narrow strip of wood
US is short for American

explanation.surface: A fruit basket is made from strips of wood packed into cases bought by an American.
explanation.definitionFit: A calathus is a vase-shaped basket of ancient Greece, a symbol of fruitfulness and often shown full of fruit.

clue.text: Burns irritates after excellent drama uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer layer is stripped off, leaving the middle letters
after places one piece behind the others in order

blocks.note: def is slang for excellent
drama is a play; take away its outer letters
something that grates irritates

explanation.surface: Annoyance at a cracking play that has been exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Drama is PLAY, and uncovering it drops the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflagrate is to burn up suddenly with intense heat, so deflagrates means burns fiercely.

clue.text: Retraction contrived showing craft of an old Greek

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A forced withdrawal reveals the cunning of an ancient Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests cunning, but here it means a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A triaconter was an ancient Greek ship with thirty oars, so it is a vessel of the Greeks.

clue.text: Chief's story that goes on further

blocks.note: a saga is a long, rambling story
more means further or additional

explanation.surface: A leader's tale that just keeps running on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: A sagamore is a chief among some Native American peoples of New England.

clue.text: Government not with it, scatty erudite banking academic rewarded

indicators.note: not with means the following word is left out
scatty means scatterbrained and disorganised, so the letters are rearranged
banking means holding in safekeeping, so these letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: G is an abbreviation for government
the word to work on, minus the next piece
taken as written, the letters to remove
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: An out-of-touch government gives a prize to a learned, scatterbrained professor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking' suggests money, but it means holding something safe inside; 'scatty' and 'not with it' both read as descriptions of the professor.
explanation.definitionFit: To guerdon is an archaic verb for giving a reward, so guerdoned means recompensed.

clue.text: Cook ham, say for old-fashioned pies

blocks.note: to bake is one way to cook
ham is an example of meat

explanation.surface: An instruction to cook ham the way the old pie makers did.
explanation.walkthrough: Bakemeat is used collectively, so it can stand for pies in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakemeat is an archaic word for pastry, a pie or baked food in general.

clue.text: Flexible fiddle lacking a string

indicators.note: lacking means missing, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: to wangle is to fiddle or obtain by trickery
a G string, as in Bach's Air on the G String

explanation.surface: A violin missing one of its strings is easily bent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a violin, but it is the verb meaning to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanle is a Scots dialect word for agile or supple, so it means pliant.

clue.text: Dock guards are rubbish

indicators.note: to guard something is to surround it protectively, so these letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: DK is an abbreviation for dock
're is the contracted form of are, as in you're

explanation.surface: Security staff at the docks are useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' looks like the verb joining the parts of the sentence, but it supplies letters in its contracted form.
explanation.definitionFit: Drek is Yiddish-derived slang for trash or worthless stuff.

clue.text: Ladies team abroad not close to Europe repeatedly?

definitions.text: Ladies team abroad not close to Europe repeatedly?

indicators.note: not means something is left out of the letters
abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to work with
the last letter of Europe, taken twice, to remove

explanation.surface: A women's side from the other side of the world, a long way from Europe again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove two Es from LADIES TEAM and rearrange. The whole clue also describes the answer: Australia is far from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Matildas are the Australian national women's football team, a ladies' side from far overseas.

clue.text: Mild oath during larkin' about?

indicators.note: larking about means fooling around, so the letters move freely

blocks.note: by means during, as in by night
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gentle curse slips out while someone is fooling around.
explanation.definitionFit: Byrlakin is an archaic minced oath, a contraction of 'by our Ladykin', meaning by the Virgin Mary.

clue.text: Yoga found a bit hard around lowest part of back

indicators.note: in a down answer the lowest part is the end, so the last letter is kept
to found metal is to melt and recast it, so the letters are reshaped
around means surrounding, so these letters go outside the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
H is short for hard, as on pencils
the final letter of back

explanation.surface: Some yoga turned out a little tough on the lower back.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhakti is devotional worship in Hinduism, and bhakti yoga is the path to union with the divine through devotion.

clue.text: Girl with tablet penning one string of verses

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so the girl's letters go around the next piece
with joins the next piece on alongside

blocks.note: a lass is a girl
I is the Roman numeral one
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A girl with an iPad writes a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The tablet looks like a computer or writing slate, but it is the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A laisse is a stanza of an Old French chanson de geste, a run of lines on one assonance.

clue.text: Old character's good in drive on reversing

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
reversing means running backwards, so the whole thing is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to hoy is to urge on or drive forward
G is short for good

explanation.surface: An old-timer is good at driving when reversing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but here it is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogh is a letter of the Middle English alphabet, used for sounds like gh and y.

clue.text: Hacks focus on the trophy at Lord's

indicators.note: the focus of a word is its centre, so the middle letter is kept

blocks.note: the middle letter of the
the Ashes is the cricket trophy contested by England and Australia; Lord's is London's famous cricket ground

explanation.surface: Journalists concentrate on the cricket trophy at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacks' looks like journalists, but it is a verb meaning chops.
explanation.definitionFit: To hash is to chop into small pieces, so hashes means cuts roughly.

clue.text: Accepted a line about the deep ocean

blocks.note: to have had something can mean to have accepted it
taken as written
L is short for line

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to a sentence about the ocean depths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a wordplay signal, but it belongs to the definition, meaning relating to.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadal describes the deepest zone of the ocean, in trenches below about 6,000 metres.

clue.text: Strange held back in fear after losing final in golf

indicators.note: after losing means something has been taken away, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: to funk is to shrink back from something out of fear
the last letter of golf, to remove

explanation.surface: A golfer bottled it on the last hole and played oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unked is a dialect word for odd, uncanny or unfamiliar, a variant of unco.

clue.text: County flags

blocks.note: first meaning: the abbreviation of Wiltshire, an English county
second meaning: droops or tires

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags' looks like a plural noun for banners, but it is a verb meaning grows weak.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiltshire is a county in south-west England, and to wilt is to droop or lose energy, like flagging.

clue.text: Mushrooms ordered from Tasmania

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Fungi sent for from the Australian island state.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanita is a genus of mushrooms including the fly agaric and the deadly death cap.

clue.text: Easily recognised vagrant kneels to grab food

indicators.note: a vagrant wanders about, so these letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
peck is slang for food, as in grub

explanation.surface: A conspicuous tramp gets down on his knees to snatch something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenspeckle is a Scots word for conspicuous, easily recognisable.

clue.text: A palm is badly treated when given end of cane

indicators.note: badly means done wrongly, so the letters are mixed up
the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
the last letter of cane

explanation.surface: A hand is hurt when it is struck with a cane at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palm' looks like the hand being caned, but it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The date palm, which bears dates, is also called a date tree.

clue.text: Ordered without doubt to protect book collection

indicators.note: to protect something is to put a shield around it, so the outer letters wrap the inner

blocks.note: indeed means certainly, without doubt
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone certainly ordered a set of books to be kept safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To indent for goods is to place an official order or requisition for them.

clue.text: Discover Japanese dishes, hot one for takeaway

indicators.note: a takeaway is something removed, so these letters are taken out

blocks.note: sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice
H is short for hot, as on taps
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Finding sushi dishes and one hot one to order as a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takeaway' looks like a food order, which suits the sushi, but it signals letters being removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To suss something out is slang for working it out or discovering the truth.
